title: Third trimester ultrasound
what: The doctor checks the baby with ultrasound late in pregnancy: growth, position, amount of fluid, and the placenta.
why: Usually at 30 to 34 weeks, as part of routine care. Sometimes more often, if your doctor orders it.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; results right away
tell_doctor: How many weeks pregnant you are
If past ultrasounds showed any problems
If you have high blood pressure, swelling, or diabetes

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat, and you do not need a full bladder.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, so your belly is easy to uncover.

steps: You lie on your back or slightly on your side
Gel is put on your belly
The doctor measures the baby's head, belly, and legs
The doctor checks the baby's position, the placenta, and the fluid
A Doppler is often done at the same time to check blood flow
feel: Cool gel and pressure from the probe on your belly
Lying on your back can make you dizzy. Say so, and you will be turned on your side
after: The report is usually ready right away
Go over the results with your own doctor at your visit
The baby's weight on ultrasound is an estimate. It can be off
red_flags: The baby moves much less: see a doctor right away
Bleeding, severe belly pain, or your water breaking: call emergency services

faq.q: Does the ultrasound show the baby's weight exactly?
faq.a: Roughly. It can be off in either direction, so the doctor looks at more than just weight.

faq.q: What if the baby is head up?
faq.a: The baby may still turn before birth. Your doctor will tell you what to do next.

reminders.text: Third trimester ultrasound tomorrow. No prep needed. Bring your pregnancy record.
